questions.stem:
Deduce the formula of each of the following ionic compounds.
(a) Aluminium oxide, formed from $Al^{3+}$ and $O^{2-}$ ions.
(b) Calcium nitrate, formed from $Ca^{2+}$ and $NO_3^{-}$ ions.
questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $Al_2O_3$ — two $Al^{3+}$ (6+) balance three $O^{2-}$ (6−).
(b) $Ca(NO_3)_2$ — one $Ca^{2+}$ (2+) balances two $NO_3^{-}$ (2−).

questions.stem: Construct the balanced chemical equation, including state symbols, for the complete combustion of methane ($CH_4$) in oxygen.

Calculate the relative molecular mass, $M_r$, of ammonium sulfate, $(NH_4)_2SO_4$.
($A_r$: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)

Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, $NH_4NO_3$.
($A_r$: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)

A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Determine its empirical formula.
($A_r$: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16)

markScheme.point: divides each percentage by $A_r$ to get moles: C $40.0/12 = 3.33$, H $6.7/1 = 6.7$, O $53.3/16 = 3.33$
divides by the smallest (3.33) to get ratio C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1

questions.modelAnswer: Moles: C $= 40.0/12 = 3.33$; H $= 6.7/1 = 6.7$; O $= 53.3/16 = 3.33$. Divide by smallest (3.33): C 1 : H 2 : O 1. Empirical formula $= CH_2O$.

questions.stem:
Magnesium burns in oxygen: $2Mg + O_2 \rightarrow 2MgO$.
Calculate the mass of magnesium oxide formed when 6.0 g of magnesium is completely burned.
($A_r$: O = 16, Mg = 24)

markScheme.point: mole ratio Mg : MgO = 1 : 1, so moles MgO = 0.25 mol

questions.modelAnswer: Moles Mg $= 6.0/24 = 0.25$ mol. From the equation moles MgO $= 0.25$ mol. $M_r(MgO) = 40$. Mass MgO $= 0.25 \times 40 = 10.0$ g.

questions.stem:
Excess hydrochloric acid is added to 10.0 g of calcium carbonate: $CaCO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow CaCl_2 + H_2O + CO_2$.
Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide produced at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.).
($A_r$: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; molar gas volume = 24 dm³ at r.t.p.)

markScheme.point: mole ratio $CaCO_3 : CO_2$ = 1 : 1, so moles $CO_2 = 0.10$ mol

questions.stem:
Hydrogen reacts with oxygen: $2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O$.
0.50 mol of hydrogen is mixed with 0.20 mol of oxygen and the reaction goes to completion.
(a) Determine the limiting reactant.
(b) Calculate the mass of water formed.
($A_r$: H = 1, O = 16)

markScheme.point: only 0.20 mol $O_2$ is available, so oxygen is the limiting reactant

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) 0.50 mol $H_2$ needs 0.25 mol $O_2$, but only 0.20 mol $O_2$ is present, so oxygen is limiting.
(b) Moles $H_2O = 2 \times 0.20 = 0.40$ mol. $M_r(H_2O) = 18$. Mass $= 0.40 \times 18 = 7.2$ g.

questions.stem:
In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution is exactly neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid: $H_2SO_4 + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2SO_4 + 2H_2O$.
Calculate the concentration of the sodium hydroxide solution in mol/dm³.
questions.modelAnswer: Moles $H_2SO_4 = 0.0200 \times 0.100 = 2.00\times10^{-3}$ mol. Ratio $H_2SO_4 : NaOH$ = 1 : 2, so moles NaOH $= 4.00\times10^{-3}$ mol. Concentration $= 4.00\times10^{-3} / 0.0250 = 0.160$ mol/dm³.

questions.stem:
When 10.0 g of calcium carbonate is heated it decomposes: $CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2$.
4.48 g of calcium oxide is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield of calcium oxide.
($A_r$: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40)

markScheme.point: moles $CaCO_3 = 10.0/100 = 0.10$ mol, so theoretical moles CaO = 0.10 mol

questions.modelAnswer: Moles $CaCO_3 = 10.0/100 = 0.10$ mol → theoretical CaO = 0.10 mol. $M_r(CaO) = 56$. Theoretical mass $= 0.10 \times 56 = 5.6$ g. % yield $= 4.48/5.6 \times 100 = 80.0\%$.
